forum.title: Broken links in "Introduction to STM32H5 security"
forum.best_answer_content:
Hello ​@JesperEC,

Thank you for your feedback, the corrections are in progress.

Best regards

Mic
forum.content_text:
[Security:Introduction to STM32H5 security - stm32mcu](https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/wiki/Security:Introduction_to_STM32H5_security) “Approved version. Approved on: 10:25, 18 May 2026”

The following links are broken:

1. In the intro section, the text “For general STM32 security see [this article](https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/wiki/Security:Security_overview) and [AN5156](https://www.st.com/content/ccc/resource/technical/document/application_note/group1/9f/0b/e4/b6/75/15/4f/e2/DM00493651/files/DM00493651.pdf/jcr:content/translations/en.DM00493651.pdf).”: The link “this article” is <https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/wiki/Security:Security_overview> which shows a “Page not found” error page.

2. In section 2, in the bullet point about PCROP, the text “Obviously this feature is redundant with the availability of TrustZone® and HDP.”: The link “TrustZone” goes to [Security:How to disable TrustZone in STM32L5xx devices during development phase - stm32mcu](https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/wiki/Security:How_to_disable_TrustZone_in_STM32L5xx_devices_during_development_phase) which is for a different MCU and not very relevant for STM32H5.

3. In section 3, the text “For introduction on these features, refer to this guide.”: The link “this guide” is <https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/index.php?title=Security:Guide_to_use_specific_security_feature&action=edit&redlink=1> - which does not exist.

4. section 3.2, the text “For broader context follow here.”: The link “here” is <https://wiki.st.com/stm32mcu/index.php?title=Security:Guide_to_use_specific_security_feature&action=edit&redlink=1> - same as above - does not exist.

5. sections 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 3.9: Same problem as 3.2

Additionally, in section 3.1, there is text “SBS effectively replaces the SYSCFG section of the STM32H5 predecessors.”. I’m pretty sure the “STM32H5” should refer to something else as this is the article about STM32H5 and AFAIK, there is no SYSCFG in H5. Maybe it should say “STM32L5" here? I don’t have any experience with that MCU though.
